pick.angle: Of 101 directories we tried, 81 offered a free option—but review queues, reciprocal-link conditions, and human verification made submission a workflow to budget for, not a backlink result to assume.
pick.why_share: Makers will share a firsthand, dated breakdown of submission outcomes and named form gotchas that helps other founders avoid wasted launch time without mistaking submissions for listings or a biased link sample for an SEO benchmark.

outline:
- **Title: "What submitting to 101 directories taught us about free listings"**
- **Opening answer block:** Lead with "81 of 101 directories offered a free option." Within the first 50 words, explain that queues, reciprocal-link conditions, and human checks make this a workflow to budget for, not a backlink result to assume.
- **## What we tested:** Identify Jason T. as the maker of AgentoolRank, a directory of open-source AI agent tools ranked by live GitHub activity. Name our submission notes as the source: 101 sites, three products, September 29 to October 2, 2026, last verified October 2. Explain the manual and browser-automation approach, one submission per site per product, without captcha-solving services.
- **## A submission is not a live listing:** Use a compact outcomes table: 66 submitted or already listed; 19 skipped for rules or fit; 9 queued for retry; 5 stopped at a visible captcha; 2 stopped over a required badge. Keep the combined "submitted or already listed" category intact, without implying 66 published listings.
- **## Free comes with conditions:** Report counts across all 101 sites: 56 put free submissions in a review queue, 14 require a badge, 12 require a backlink, and 1 requires an X post. Ground the waiting-time discussion in Viesearch's 1,200+ queue and stated 82% free-tier rejection rate, SaaSHub's up-to-32-day wait, and TinyLaunch's scheduled November 2 launch. Note that 39 sites showed a price, with a $12 median entry price.
- **## Budget for human steps and uncertain confirmations:** Cover 30 sites needing inbox access, 19 offering or requiring Google login, and 8 having a captcha requiring a person. Distinguish captcha presence from the 5 captcha-stopped outcomes. Explain why automation needs follow-up: only 75 sites showed a clear confirmation.
- **## Small form details change the workflow:** Describe FutureTools' "No thanks" popup dismissal, SaaSHub's need to claim management access before closing the browser, Viesearch's spam-folder check and waiting-list clicks, and Findly.tools' ongoing footer-badge condition. Tie these to a per-site log of dates, results, and blockers.
- **## Check the link before counting it:** Present the deliberately limited rel-attribute check: 30 nonrandom sites, usually inspected when something looked off; 23 nofollow, 6 dofollow, 1 ugc. Use AlternativeTo, LaunchBoosts, make.rs, and AI Agents Directory only for their documented link attributes or conditions. Do not extrapolate to all 101 sites or claim SEO gains.
- **## Stars measure attention, downloads measure use:** Reserve about 120 words near the end for current figures checked on [the downloads page](https://agentoolrank.com/downloads) when drafting. Explain npm downloads API plus pypistats, the registry-to-repository matching requirement, and why CI and mirrors make downloads a usage signal rather than a user count. Do not reuse the October 3 figures.
- **## What to do before your next submission:** Close with concrete actions: read free-tier conditions before filling forms, budget for inbox and captcha steps, inspect live-link attributes, and log submissions to avoid duplicates. State that we saw very little referral traffic so far, without a number or traffic promise.
- **Closing lines:** Link our [free comparison of where to list an AI agent tool](https://agentoolrank.com/where-to-list), then invite corrections: "If a site's rules changed, tell us and we update the data." Follow with one plain line about our [Submit Kit](https://agentoolrank.com/submit-kit): product-type rankings, form gotchas, a don't-submit list, top 10 free over MCP, full list $29 one-time. Sign "Jason T." and finish with a short ownership disclosure.

Run automation when someone can handle verification, rather than treating it as unattended overnight work.

If a launch date is too late, do not spend the session preparing that submission.
